'''''Hura polyandra''''' is a species of tree native to various parts of [[Latin America]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Hura polyandra Baill. {{!}} Plants of the World Online {{!}} Kew Science |url=http://powo.science.kew.org/taxon/urn:lsid:ipni.org:names:350061-1 |access-date=2022-12-29 |website=Plants of the World Online |language=en}}</ref>

In 2019 the [[IUCN Red List|IUCN]] classified this species as least concern due to there being no recent evidence of  significant threats or future ones, as well as its large distribution and population.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Hura polyandra |url=https://www.iucnredlist.org/species/62003558/149008229 |access-date=29 December 2022 |website=[[IUCN Red List]]}}</ref>

Trees can grow up to 30 meters in height<ref name=":0" /> and its flowers are [[Monoecy|monoecious]] with absent petals.<ref>{{Cite book |last1=AZ |first1=Tucson Richard Stephen Felger Executive Director Drylands Institute |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=tvk5FN3L-Q0C&dq=hura+polyandra&pg=PA149 |title=The Trees of Sonora, Mexico |last2=Program |first2=University of Arizona Matthew Brian Johnson Program Manager and Curator Desert Legume |last3=AZ |first3=Tucson Michael Francis Wilson Research Director Drylands Institute |date=2001-03-31 |publisher=Oxford University Press, USA |isbn=978-0-19-976127-2 |pages=149 |language=en}}</ref> The species occurs in cleared agricultural areas, forest plains, and rocky hillsides.<ref name=":0" />
